questions.question: What is the name of Nintendo's famous plumber?
questions.fact: Mario was first called "Jumpman" when he appeared in Donkey Kong in 1981.

questions.question: What colour is Luigi's cap?
questions.fact: Luigi was first made by changing Mario's colours, and he's usually a bit taller.

questions.question: In which game do you build with blocks and avoid exploding Creepers?
questions.fact: Minecraft was created by Swedish programmer Markus "Notch" Persson. Microsoft bought it in 2014.

questions.question: What does Pac-Man eat as he goes through the maze?
questions.fact: Pac-Man's shape was reportedly inspired by a pizza with a slice missing.

questions.question: What is the name of Sonic's two-tailed fox friend?
questions.fact: Tails's real name is Miles Prower, a pun on "miles per hour".

questions.question: Which company makes the Xbox?
questions.fact: The first Xbox came out in 2001. Its name started as a nickname for a "DirectX box".

questions.question: What is the best-selling video game of all time?
questions.fact: Minecraft has sold over 300 million copies across all its versions.

questions.question: In which game do you rotate falling blocks to clear lines?
questions.fact: Tetris's name mixes "tetra" (four, as each piece has four squares) and tennis, its creator's favourite sport.

questions.question: Tetris was created in which country?
questions.fact: Alexey Pajitnov made Tetris in 1984 in Moscow. He didn't earn money from it for years.

questions.question: In chess, which piece can only move diagonally?
questions.fact: Each player has two bishops, one that stays on light squares and one on dark squares.

questions.question: Which chess piece moves in an L shape?
questions.fact: The knight is the only chess piece that can jump over other pieces.

questions.question: How many squares are on a chessboard?
questions.fact: The number of possible chess games is bigger than the number of atoms in the observable universe.

questions.question: In classic Monopoly, how much do you collect for passing GO?
questions.fact: Monopoly grew out of "The Landlord's Game", invented in 1904 by Lizzie Magie to show the problems with greedy landlords.

questions.question: How many dice are used in Monopoly?
questions.fact: Rolling doubles three times in a row in Monopoly sends you straight to jail.

questions.question: How many tiles does each Scrabble player hold?
questions.fact: Using all seven tiles in one go in Scrabble is a "bingo" and earns 50 bonus points.

questions.question: Which word game uses a 15 x 15 board and letter tiles?
questions.fact: Scrabble was invented in the 1930s by an out-of-work architect, Alfred Butts.

questions.question: In which game do you try to sink your opponent's ships?
questions.fact: Battleship started as a pencil-and-paper game, long before the plastic board version.

questions.question: What are you trying to solve in Cluedo?
questions.fact: Cluedo was invented in England in the 1940s. In the US it's simply called "Clue".

questions.question: Which one-player card game is also called "Patience"?
questions.fact: Solitaire came free with Windows from 1990 partly to teach people how to use a mouse.

questions.question: How many cards are in a standard deck, without jokers?
questions.fact: 52 cards are often said to match the weeks in a year, but there's no proof it was planned that way.

questions.question: How many cards are in the most common Spanish deck?
questions.fact: The Spanish deck has no 8s or 9s and goes 1 to 7, then sota, caballo and rey.

questions.question: What are the four suits of a Spanish deck?
questions.fact: Spanish suits are oros, copas, espadas and bastos, used in games like mus, brisca and tute.

questions.question: Which Nintendo console can be played handheld or docked to a TV?
questions.fact: The Switch came out in 2017 and has sold over 140 million units.

questions.question: In Fortnite, what do players jump out of to reach the island?
questions.fact: The Battle Bus flies over the island hanging from a big blue hot-air balloon.

questions.question: Which princess does Mario usually rescue?
questions.fact: Princess Peach was called "Princess Toadstool" in English-speaking countries until 1993.

questions.question: What is the name of the hero in "The Legend of Zelda"?
questions.fact: Many people think the hero is called Zelda, but Zelda is the princess. The hero is Link.

questions.question: What type of Pokémon is Charmander?
questions.fact: Charmander evolves into Charmeleon and then Charizard.

questions.question: What is the person who runs a Dungeons & Dragons game called?
questions.fact: Dungeons & Dragons was first published in 1974 and is still hugely popular today.

questions.question: Which game is played on a table with a cue and balls?
questions.fact: Pool, snooker and billiards are different cue sports; snooker uses 22 balls.

questions.question: What is the most you can score with a single dart?
questions.fact: 60 is the triple 20, a tiny strip at the top of the dartboard.

questions.question: What is the maximum score with three darts?
questions.fact: 180 needs three darts in the triple 20, and darts commentators famously shout "One hundred and eightyyy!"

questions.question: Which board game says "Go directly to Jail"?
questions.fact: Monopoly's jail is in the corner. If you're "just visiting", you don't have to pay to get out.

questions.question: Which board game has resources like wood, brick and sheep?
questions.fact: Catan was created by German designer Klaus Teuber in 1995 and has sold over 40 million copies.

questions.question: Which tile-laying board game is named after a walled French city?
questions.fact: Carcassonne is a real medieval walled city in southern France.

questions.question: The board game "Azul" is inspired by which Portuguese art?
questions.fact: Azul was inspired by "azulejos", the painted tiles found all over Portugal and Spain.

questions.question: Which company makes the Grand Theft Auto series?
questions.fact: Rockstar Games is based in New York, but the GTA series began in Scotland, at DMA Design.

questions.question: Which football video game series was renamed "EA Sports FC"?
questions.fact: EA's FIFA licence ended in 2023, after almost 30 years, so the series became "EA Sports FC".

questions.question: In "Among Us", what are the hidden traitors called?
questions.fact: Among Us came out in 2018 but only became a huge hit in 2020, during lockdowns.

questions.question: What is the name of the heroine of "Tomb Raider"?
questions.fact: Angelina Jolie played Lara Croft in the films, starting in 2001.

questions.question: Which "Street Fighter" character is famous for the "Hadouken" fireball?
questions.fact: Ryu has been in every main Street Fighter game since the first one in 1987.

questions.question: Which game has you fling birds at pigs?
questions.fact: Angry Birds was made by Rovio, a company from Finland, and came out in 2009.

questions.question: Which mobile game has you match colourful sweets?
questions.fact: Candy Crush Saga came out in 2012 and has been downloaded billions of times.

questions.question: In "The Sims", what is the green diamond above a Sim's head called?
questions.fact: A "plumbob" is a tool for checking if walls are straight. Its colour shows your Sim's mood.

questions.question: What is the money in "The Sims" called?
questions.fact: "Simoleon" is old American slang for a dollar, possibly a mix of "simon" and "Napoleon".

questions.question: What money does Link collect in "The Legend of Zelda"?
questions.fact: Zelda's money shares its name with India's currency, the rupee.

questions.question: Which company created Pac-Man?
questions.fact: Namco was a Japanese company; Pac-Man came out in 1980 and was called "Puck Man" in Japan.

questions.question: Which fighting game is famous for the phrase "Finish him!"?
questions.fact: The age ratings used on video games today were partly a reaction to Mortal Kombat's violence.

questions.question: What is Mario's job?
questions.fact: Mario was first a carpenter in Donkey Kong. He became a plumber in Mario Bros. in 1983.

questions.question: Which villain keeps kidnapping Princess Peach?
questions.fact: Bowser's Japanese name is "Kuppa", taken from a Korean dish.

questions.question: Who is Sonic's main villain?
questions.fact: Dr. Eggman's original name in the West was Dr. Robotnik.

questions.question: In chess, what is it called when the king is attacked and cannot escape?
questions.fact: "Checkmate" comes from the Persian "shāh māt", usually translated as "the king is helpless".

questions.question: What is the chess move where the king and a rook swap sides called?
questions.fact: Castling is the only move in chess where two pieces move at once.

questions.question: In UNO, what must you shout when you have one card left?
questions.fact: If you forget to shout "UNO!" and get caught, you have to draw two cards.

questions.question: In which game are numbers drawn at random until someone completes a line or card?
questions.fact: Bingo became popular in Spain in the 1970s, and bingo halls are still common today.

questions.question: How many dots are on a standard six-sided die in total?
questions.fact: Opposite sides of a die always add up to 7.

questions.question: How many tiles are in a standard double-six domino set?
questions.fact: Dominoes probably came from China, and the game is hugely popular in Spain and Latin America.

questions.question: Which Japanese company started in 1889 by making playing cards?
questions.fact: Nintendo's first product was hand-made "hanafuda" playing cards, and it still sells them in Japan.

questions.question: Which 1972 arcade game was a simple version of table tennis?
questions.fact: Pong was made by Atari in 1972 and is often called the first commercially successful video game.

questions.question: Which classic arcade game has rows of aliens moving down the screen?
questions.fact: Space Invaders was so popular in Japan that it's often said to have caused a 100-yen coin shortage, though that's probably a myth.

questions.question: In "Animal Crossing", which raccoon sells you your house?
questions.fact: Tom Nook is a tanuki, a Japanese raccoon dog, not really a raccoon.

questions.question: Which game series has the slogan "Gotta catch 'em all"?
questions.fact: Pokémon is short for "Pocket Monsters". It started with two Game Boy games in 1996.

questions.question: In Monopoly, what is the most expensive property on the classic UK board?
questions.fact: Mayfair costs £400 on the UK board. On the Spanish Monopoly board, the top spot is Paseo del Prado.
